Listen to this article Share Nigeria’s Super Eagles suffered a setback in their bid to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) after being held to a disappointing 0-0 draw against Tanzania at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar on Tuesday. Advertisement Advertisement The result denied Eric Chelle’s side an opportunity to strengthen their position in Group L, leaving them level on seven points with leaders Guinea-Bissau, who have a game in hand. Despite dominating possession and creating several scoring opportunities, Nigeria failed to break down a disciplined Tanzania side, with both teams also hitting the woodwork. The Super Eagles came closest to opening the scoring in the 34th minute when striker Tolu Arokodare beat Tanzania goalkeeper Aishi Manula with a low effort, only for his shot to strike the post. Moses Usor threatened four minutes later, forcing Manula into a save, while defender Calvin Bassey sent an effort narrowly over the crossbar. Chelle made seven changes to the team that secured a 3-1 victory over Tanzania in Uyo on Friday, but the alterations failed to produce the desired result. Advertisement Nigeria continued to push for a winner, with Manula denying Usor, Abdullahi Bewene and Akor Adams. Tanzania also created opportunities, as Simon Msuva struck the post before half-time, while Stanley Nwabali saved an effort from Iddy Nado after the break. Guinea-Bissau hold qualification advantage The draw leaves Nigeria second in Group L on seven points, behind Guinea-Bissau, who have the same tally but a game in hand. Madagascar and Tanzania have two points each. Advertisement Tanzania’s position in the group is different from Nigeria’s, as the Taifa Stars have already secured qualification as co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda. This leaves only one available qualification spot for the remaining teams in Group L. Guinea-Bissau could strengthen their grip on the group with victory over Madagascar in their outstanding fixture. A win would take them to 10 points, three clear of Nigeria with two rounds of matches remaining. Advertisement Advertisement If Guinea-Bissau win their next two home fixtures, they would secure the group’s remaining qualification ticket, leaving Nigeria with little margin for error. The Super Eagles are therefore likely to need victories in their remaining matches against Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau to keep their qualification hopes firmly in their hands. With two rounds remaining in March, Nigeria must now deliver stronger performances to avoid missing out on another major continental tournament.
